newsitem.title: USA: Medical Graphics sees 1997 EPS over $0.10.
newsitem.headline: Medical Graphics sees 1997 EPS over $0.10.

text.p: Medical Graphics Corp president and chief executive officer Eric Sivertson said Tuesday the company's earnings per share in 1997 would exceed $0.10.
"We will do better than $0.10 per share next year. I would be disappointed if we did $0.10," he said told Reuters after a Dain Bosworth healthcare conference presentation.
But Sivertson declined to comment on First Call's consensus estimate of a loss of $0.45 per share in 1996.
In 1995, the company lost $0.71 per share.
Sivertson told investors to expect continued aggressive pricing by the company.
"Until we get our cost programs going, we will continue with our aggressive pricing strategy. We expect to have the cost programs in place in six-to-nine months."
In the second quarter, the St. Paul, Minnesota manufacturer of cardiorespiratory diagnostic systems saw a four percent drop in revenues on a 10 percent increase in unit volume sales.
Sivertson told Reuters the company was working to improve its costs of service and supply.

"We need to do a better job of training people out in the field. Eighty percent of the questions that come into our customer service center are 'How do I do this?' questions. We're spending a lot of time and money training and re-training. We've got to become more efficient," he said.
The executive said he expects slight increases in general and administration costs.

"I think we've leveled off the G&A cost changes. I've got two more people to hire, so it's going to go up a little bit more, but then we will have achieved critical mass, having the right people in the right jobs."

Sivertson also told Reuters increases in research and development spending will have to wait until Medical Graphics has improved sales. In 1995, the company spent $1.9 million on research and development.
